findings.reason: a node implementing the change as written would silently move a second store it was neither told about nor scoped to verify, and the plan's write-path list would be incomplete.
findings.text: §2 says "The `pick-input` kind gets its own leaf under the cache root instead of the root itself (`reckon/_store.py:162`)", but that leaf is shared by two stores: `reckon/capabilities.py:1190` also resolves `_store.cache_root("pick-input")` for its `picker-<name>.json` files, so changing the leaf at `_store.py:162` relocates the picker-input cache as well as the ledger indexes, and `reckon/capabilities.py` is not among §2's declared write paths

findings.reason: the node would ship a shared index that re-runs the full aggregate load on each alternation between checkouts, so the sharing delivers one file but not the cached re-read the change exists to provide, and nothing in the done-when would catch it.
findings.text: §2 makes a worktree and its main checkout "share one index file", but the index's freshness stamp stays per-checkout: `index_stamp` (`reckon/ledger.py:902-916`) and `aggregate_stamp` (`reckon/ledger.py:1076`) key on `_file_identity(ledger_path(project, root))`, and `_file_identity` (`reckon/ledger.py:850-855`) returns `(st_mtime_ns, st_ctime_ns, st_size, st_ino)` — the inode — so two checkouts with distinct ledger files (which is why `ledger_path` resolves under each checkout) produce distinct stamps and each invalidates the other's cached aggregate on every handoff

findings.reason: the gate cannot fail for the side effect the change introduces, so the node ships the picker-cache relocation unmeasured.
findings.text: §2's done-when builds "a temporary cache root seeded with three old-location files and one recent new-location index" and asserts the real `~/.cache/reckon` is untouched, so it exercises only `ledger-*.sqlite` paths and passes regardless of whether the `picker-*.json` cache relocation caused by the leaf change is handled
